# `spell/unknown-word`

**Every word of prose is in a word list**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-spell` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-spell` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX, Python, JSON, YAML, TOML, Markdown, CSS, SCSS, HTML |
| **Turned on by** | `codelaw:spell/strict` at `warn` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | none — severity only |
| **Fix** | `suggest` — `codelaw fix --unsafe` applies it; review the diff, it can change behaviour (a word no list holds is often a real name, a product or a term of the trade; the nearest dictionary word is a guess the author confirms) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.3.0 |

## What it checks

A word in a comment, a docstring, a prose string, Markdown text, HTML text or an HTML `alt`, `title`, `aria-label` or `placeholder`, or a string value of JSON, YAML or TOML is in no word list: not in the pack's dictionary (SCOWL's US and British English up to size 60, with every form written out, plus the software terms), not on the known-typo list (`spell/known-typo` reports those) and not in `[spell] words`. A word in capitals is an acronym and is not checked; so are words shorter than four letters and every token `spell/known-typo` skips (URLs, paths, identifiers, hashes, template tags); a text that is not English, as `spell/known-typo` judges it, is not checked.

**Why:** the known-typo list catches the misspellings codelaw can predict; the dictionary catches the rest (`seperately`, `responce`). It is in `spell/strict`, not `spell/recommended`, because code is full of real words no dictionary holds.

The fix replaces the word with the nearest dictionary word: fewest edits (Damerau-Levenshtein, at most two, the first letter kept), then the commoner word, then alphabetical order. The message names up to three.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-spell
pip install codelaw-rules-spell
```

**Then extend a preset that turns it on** — `codelaw:spell/strict` sets it to `warn`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:spell/strict"]
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"spell/unknown-word" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — a scope of your own needs `files`:

```toml
[scope.legacy]
files = ["src/legacy/**/*.js"]
rules = { "spell/unknown-word" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"spell/unknown-word" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"spell/unknown-word" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"spell/unknown-word" = { severity = "warn" }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "spell/unknown-word": {"severity": "warn"}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JavaScript:** `// codelaw-ignore spell/unknown-word: <reason>`
- **Python:** `# codelaw-ignore spell/unknown-word: <reason>`
- **JSON** has no comments: switch the rule off for the file with a scope, or use the baseline.
- **Markdown:** `<!-- codelaw-ignore spell/unknown-word: <reason> -->`
- **CSS:** `/* codelaw-ignore spell/unknown-word: <reason> */`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore spell/unknown-word expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule spell/unknown-word --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain spell/unknown-word       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule spell/unknown-word  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>      # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. If the word is misspelled, run `codelaw fix --unsafe` to take the first suggestion, or write the word the message names that you meant.
2. If the word is right (a name, a product, a term of your trade), add it to the root `codelaw.toml`: `[spell]` `words = ["kubectl"]`. `spell/suspicious-word` checks the list.
3. For a one-off, excuse the line: `// codelaw-ignore spell/unknown-word: <reason>`.

## Examples

### JavaScript

#### Don't

```js
// Retry seperately until it works.
```

#### Do

```js
// Retry separately until it works.
```

### JSX

#### Don't

```jsx
const Hint = () => <p>Retry seperately until it works</p>;
```

#### Do

```jsx
const Hint = () => <p>Retry separately until it works</p>;
```

### TypeScript

#### Don't

```ts
// Retry seperately until it works.
```

#### Do

```ts
// Retry separately until it works.
```

### TSX

#### Don't

```tsx
const Hint = (): JSX.Element => <p>Retry seperately until it works</p>;
```

#### Do

```tsx
const Hint = (): JSX.Element => <p>Retry separately until it works</p>;
```

### Python

#### Don't

```python
def run():
    """Retry seperately until it works."""
```

#### Do

```python
def run():
    """Retry separately until it works."""
```

### JSON

#### Don't

```json
{ "description": "Retry seperately until it works" }
```

#### Do

```json
{ "description": "Retry separately until it works" }
```

### YAML

#### Don't

```yaml
# Retry seperately until it works.
summary: Retry seperately until it works
```

#### Do

```yaml
# Retry separately until it works.
summary: Retry separately until it works
```

### TOML

#### Don't

```toml
# Retry seperately until it works.
```

#### Do

```toml
# Retry separately until it works.
```

### Markdown

#### Don't

```md
Retry seperately until it works.
```

#### Do

```md
Retry separately until it works.
```

### CSS

#### Don't

```css
/* Retry seperately until it works. */
.box { color: red; }
```

#### Do

```css
/* Retry separately until it works. */
.box { color: red; }
```

### SCSS

#### Don't

```scss
// Retry seperately until it works.
.box { color: red; }
```

#### Do

```scss
// Retry separately until it works.
.box { color: red; }
```

### HTML

#### Don't

```html
<p title="Retry seperately">Retry until it works</p>
```

#### Do

```html
<p title="Retry separately">Retry until it works</p>
```
